name: HalfSyncHalfAsync
summary: Decomposes concurrent processing into a synchronous layer and an asynchronous one, with a queueing layer between them, so simplicity and responsiveness are each paid for where they are worth it.

reference.author: Douglas Schmidt, Michael Stal, Hans Rohnert, Frank Buschmann

roles.name: SynchronousTaskLayer
roles.summary: Where the high-level work happens, in threads of its own that may block: it has a stack and registers, so it can be written as a sequence of steps and read as one. Everything easy to follow in the system lives here, and it is here that the thread count is paid for.

roles.name: AsynchronousTaskLayer
roles.summary: Where the low-level work happens, driven by events from outside and never blocking, because it has no stack of its own to block on. A blocking call added here does not slow the layer down — it stops the system taking events at all.

roles.name: QueueingLayer
roles.summary: The buffering and notification point between the two layers, in both directions. It is the only place they meet, which is what makes the decomposition real rather than a diagram: a direct call across it puts one layer's blocking into the other's thread.
